Text:
Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral at 1 Cong Xa Paris is a religious architectural landmark in the District 1 area. Consider its exterior form alongside its construction history and role in worship. It is a religious space in use, so visits require respect for religious activities.

Vietnam's national tourism authority dates construction to 1877–1880. From outside, notice the brick walls, arched openings and twin bell towers. Try viewing the building from different safe positions and compare the details with the dated photographs in this guide.

Beyond the twin towers, notice the central façade clock and the Our Lady of Peace statue in the forecourt. Move from the overall outline to its central accents, then to the space between the street and worship area. Compare the brick walls and arched openings from different positions.

Use the dated captions when comparing photographs. This guide includes earlier views and restoration images; neither proves the current condition or an open entrance. Respect restricted areas, consult the managing institution's notices and move safely around the square.

Before visiting, check the cathedral’s notices about services and access. If the interior is unavailable to visitors, explore the exterior instead. Remain quiet, keep entrances clear and avoid photographs that disturb people at prayer.
